correctness.rationale: Characteristic-two coordinate change sends the symmetric six-coordinate cubic to a projective cone over S: F(y)=sum_i y_i^3+(sum_i y_i)^3. Its partial derivatives (y_i+sum y)^2 cannot vanish simultaneously projectively, so S is a smooth cubic surface. Projection from the cone vertex separates the S-family of lines through the vertex from 27 plane-dual families of nonvertex lines. A Grassmannian chart gives the base equation and transverse linear/quasilinear quadratic/cubic equations. Generic independence and nonvanishing of the cubic coefficient lead over algebraic closure of k(S) to the complete intersection Kbar[u,v]/(u²,v³) of length 6 and Hilbert function (1,2,2,1). Independently coded RREF projective-line enumeration found S-lines (15,27) and cone-lines (75,477) at q=2,4. Independent F32 arithmetic verified s=(1,2,6,16),w=(0,1,22,31): F(s)=A1=A2=0, F(w)=19 !=0, the two transverse linear forms independent. Frobenius line permutation yields 15 fixed+6 transpositions, Picard trace 5 and stated point counts/zeta for all n. Explicit genericity witness verifies open condition; finite tests alone do not prove general geometry.
